observation.visible_scene: High-angle/aerial view of a very wide waterfall (Victoria Falls–like). A broad, sun-glinting river flows along the right and top of frame and pours over a long cliff lip into a dark gorge on the left. A tall plume of white mist/spray billows up from the gorge on the left side, with a faint rainbow band embedded in it. Foreground bottom-right shows a dark rocky outcrop with green vegetation; upstream islands and tree-lined banks sit across the top. The shot is essentially a fixed aerial framing of this scene.
visible_changes: The curtain of falling water over the lip shows continuous downward streaking and churning; the pattern of white water shifts frame to frame while the lip's position stays fixed (flow, not translation of the cliff).
The river surface on the right keeps shimmering as ripples move the sun reflections; the bright glint zone stays roughly in place (reflection change, not separate moving objects).

The mist plume on the left deforms and billows: its internal brightness and warm glow vary, and its edges expand/contract slightly over time (expansion/deformation of the spray cloud, not a translating object).

The faint rainbow within the left mist varies in visibility/intensity across the segment—barely discernible early, with slightly stronger colored bands (green/reddish) appearing in some later frames—tracking the changing mist density, not a new object.
The rocky outcrop, cliff edge, upstream islands and overall composition remain in the same image positions throughout, indicating little to no camera translation or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera drifts or pans before/after this cropped segment.
The cause of the changing mist density and rainbow intensity (e.g., wind, sun angle) is not shown.
What happens downstream in the gorge or beyond the top river bend is not visible.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: background landmarks (cliff lip, outcrop, islands) hold nearly constant positions, so the framing looks static, but a very slight slow drift cannot be fully excluded.
The apparent strengthening of the rainbow may be partly a lighting/mist effect rather than a true change in the rainbow itself.
